analysis:
Examined all supplied ci.yml excerpts and complete changed-line ranges. Head lines 53–64 add conditional macOS Sandbox routing; provider shards, summary, SDK, cluster metadata and runtime jobs now depend on route and consume its runner outputs (232–234, 477–479, 675–677, 878–880, 1010–1012). BASE lines 1053–1202 establish the prior fixed-runner GPU/focused jobs and fail-closed Provider Tests result checks; their HEAD replacements and gate are outside these excerpts.
No concrete regression is established locally: classification predicates remain aligned with lane selection, workflow permissions remain contents:read, checkout does not persist credentials, and explicit cache saves remain restricted to master/dev pushes. The range map shows no changes to native test commands, artifact collection, cache controls or suite auditing in the supplied HEAD scope. Cache-disable settings at 403–414 are test-only, not changes to T-041 production isolation or encryption. No serving authorization, attestation, plaintext handling or billing implementation is changed here.
Material integration question: .github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml and its provisioning dependencies must establish who controls the newly selected Macs, isolation and cleanup between adversarial PRs and trusted pushes, binding of runner labels to the allocated lane, and fallback/failure behavior. Newly routed jobs can execute repository code, save trusted-branch build caches (271–282, 974–985), and produce native/security test evidence. If hosts are provider-controlled, test-result integrity and cross-run contamination need explicit treatment; this excerpt does not establish that prerequisite or a missing control. Reconcile this CI execution boundary with A-019/TB-013 and artifact/qualification assumptions A-017/T-054/T-056 without treating CI success as serving qualification. Verify remaining HEAD GPU/focused jobs and the aggregate gate against BASE 1170–1202. Only selected threat definitions were supplied in full.
